prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a sideswipe while changing lanes in Katy, Texas, and has neck and back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1497; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Can you confirm you're comfortable with us recording this call?

A: Yes, that's fine.

Q: Please describe where the accident happened.

A: It was on a multi-lane road in Katy, Texas, in the right lane heading toward the freeway on-ramp area. Traffic was moderate and moving steadily.

Q: What were you doing right before the collision?

A: I was changing lanes to the left because I needed to get over for a turn coming up. I checked my mirror, I saw the lane looked clear, and I signaled and started to move over.

Q: Did you see the other vehicle at any point before contact?

A: Not directly. I glanced at my left mirror and didn't see anything right next to me. Then I felt a hard bump on my left side and heard scraping metal. My car pushed to the right and I had to correct the steering.

Q: Did the other driver say anything at the scene?

A: They got out and said they had been in my blind spot and that they tried to swerve. We exchanged information and the police were called.

Q: Did you or anyone else require medical attention?

A: I was checked out at an urgent care clinic later that afternoon. My neck is stiff and sore, and my lower back has been aching since the impact. The doctor diagnosed a neck and back strain and gave me some medication and a referral for physical therapy.

Q: Are you currently still experiencing symptoms?

A: Yes, the stiffness is worse in the mornings and sitting for long periods makes my back hurt. I have an appointment for therapy next week.

Q: Is there anything else you think we should know?

A: Just that I'm cooperating fully and I have photos of both vehicles that I can send you.

Q: Thank you. That concludes the statement.

A: Okay, thank you.
